item.content:encoded:
Monitoring legal regulation of the digital economy

发布源: 32. Gaidar Institute for Economic Policy, FKA Institute for the Economy in Transition --Russia | 抓取时间: 2026-10-28

Starting from 2024, Gaidar Institute launched a monthly review of international trends in the legal regulation of the digital economy. The purpose of Monitoring is to timely identify key developments and trends in the global practice of regulating the digital sector. The scientific and expert analysis allows not only to track current changes, but also to forecast their potential impact on the development of the digital industry in our country, contributing to the formation of an adaptive and effective strategy of legal regulation in this area.

It is published in Russian and English.

Full versionof the article

Over the past two centuries, the extent to which societies around the world are interconnected and influence one another has increased many times over. Digital, energy, and logistics networks span the globe. Undersea cables, data centers, satellite constellations, power grids, energy pipelines, water supply systems, and the technologies and algorithms that run them together constitute a shared space for humanity. Much of today’s global infrastructure is the legacy of the extraordinary advances in science and technology during the second half of the 20th century and the first quarter of the 21st. Despite persistent declarations that globalization is coming to an end, it is not disappearing but continues to expand as trade grows and new waves of scientific and technological progress unfold.

However, the nature of globalization is changing: the balance is shifting once again, both among the interests of key actors (states, transnational corporations, and others) and among and within globalization’s various components.
